verdict.rationale: Bento's own docs describe AI-driven insights from the user's trace data inside the product: plain-English signals trained on the user's own traces, automatic clustering of similar findings, AI judgment of whether each alert incident is real or benign, and pinpointing what shifted when agent behavior drifts. The suggestion side is thinner: fixes and nudges are shadow-tested and promoted, but the docs never say plainly that Bento generates these suggestions itself. All evidence is vendor-claimed. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that Bento AI-generates fix suggestions or recommendations, detail on how insights are presented in the UI, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can get AI-generated insights and suggestions from my data inside the product

citations.quote: Describe any failure mode in plain English — Bento trains a signal on your own traces, fires it in real time, and backfills your entire history
Similar findings group into clusters, so patterns surface before you go looking.
Bento groups fires into incidents and judges each one real or benign — so you only wake up for real drift.
See when your agent starts behaving differently — Bento pinpoints exactly what shifted.
Reusable, trigger-based fixes: skills, subagents, and tools that graduate from candidate to promote as they prove themselves in production.
A living memory of what your agent has learned — every failure pattern, fix, and outcome, in plain language.
